_comment: SCAFFOLD. Correct shape, real but incomplete entries. This is not yet a two person labelling of the screenplay and the recall figures it produces are not publishable. Completing it is item 9 of the README build status. See README.md in this directory for the protocol.
_dedup_note: Every mention becomes a span and the ledger collapses them. A character named through eight scenes is one research subject with many occurrence pointers, and the ratio is the single biggest lever on both cost and report readability.

seeded_claims.claim_text: The Air Ministry refused her a licence in 1931.
seeded_claims.why: Planted falsehood. Contradicted on the page by Davies, and by the record. This is the red line the demo clicks.
Atomic decomposition. The count is a separate claim from the refusal and must verify independently, exactly as a complaint itemises alleged falsehoods.

seeded_claims.claim_text: She has never flown a night leg alone.
seeded_claims.why: Plausible, and the record says nothing either way. Amber, and the category that settles.

seeded_claims.claim_text: She was the first woman to hold a first class navigator's certificate in this country in 1933.
seeded_claims.why: True and surprising. Proves the system is not a paranoia engine.

seeded_claims.claim_text: She flew Croydon to Le Bourget in November, in the dark, alone.
seeded_claims.why: Directly rebuts SEED-003 within the scene. Two claims about the same subject reaching different verdicts is the granularity the product sells.
Characterisation. Defamation law protects opinion, so it must be classified, coloured grey, and never researched. Spending a cent on this is a failure.

expected_summary._comment: Approximate targets for the labelled script. Dense enough to impress, sparse enough that every red line on screen is legible and damning.
